provider_was_disposed.error: ProviderException: The provider was disposed before it could return a value
causes: Provider is autoDispose and last listener was removed
Parent widget unmounted during async operation

solutions.approach: Check if mounted before state update

memory_leak_video.symptom: App crashes with OOM (Out of Memory) after scrolling videos

solution.explanation: Provider auto-disposes when widget unmounts, triggering controller.dispose()

excessive_rebuilds.symptom: Widget rebuilds too frequently, poor performance
causes: Watching entire object when only one field needed
Using ref.watch inside build without select

solutions.solution: Combine providers or use select to isolate dependencies

solution.mechanism: New query creates new provider instance, old instance disposed → client.close() → request cancelled

firestore_read_costs.symptom: High Firebase billing from document reads
causes: autoDispose stream recreated on every navigation
User navigating back and forth triggers new snapshots

async_loading_flicker.symptom: List disappears and shows loading spinner on refresh
async_loading_flicker.cause: Setting state to AsyncLoading without preserving previous data

solution.explanation: Preserves current data while fetching, UI shows data + loading indicator

onesignal_navigation_before_app_ready.symptom: Notification clicked before app initialized, navigation fails

solution.ui_integration: ConsumerWidget wraps app, shows splash until appStartupProvider completes

family_parameters_not_updating.symptom: Provider family not re-creating when parameters change
causes: Passing mutable objects instead of immutable

solutions.good: class Filter { final bool isActive; const Filter(this.isActive); }

solutions.code:
@override bool operator ==(Object other) => identical(this, other) || other is Filter && isActive == other.isActive;
@override int get hashCode => isActive.hashCode;

ref_watch_in_async.error: Cannot call ref.watch inside an async gap
ref_watch_in_async.cause: Using ref.watch after an await statement

solution.explanation: ref.watch must be called synchronously in build() or top of methods

state_not_persisting.cause: Provider is autoDispose and was disposed during navigation
solutions: Move state to higher-level provider that survives navigation
Use @Riverpod(keepAlive: true) if state should persist app-wide

reduce_rebuild_scope.technique: Use select() to watch specific fields
reduce_rebuild_scope.impact: Reduces rebuilds by 70-90% in complex objects

batch_state_updates.technique: Update state once with combined result
batch_state_updates.bad: state = newValue1; state = newValue2; state = newValue3;

lazy_initialization.pattern: Use FutureProvider with autoDispose, only created when watched

stream_distinct.technique: Riverpod 3.0 automatically uses == to filter duplicates
stream_distinct.impact: High-frequency streams (Firestore metadata updates) don't trigger rebuilds
stream_distinct.note: Ensure your models implement == operator correctly

inspect_provider_state.approach: Read provider value in debug console

statenotifier_ref_access.problem: StateNotifier can't access ref in constructor
statenotifier_ref_access.riverpod_3_solution: Use Notifier, ref available as this.ref in build()

family_tuple_complexity.problem: Multiple parameters required complex tuple logic
family_tuple_complexity.riverpod_3: @riverpod Type name(Ref ref, {required String id, int limit = 20})

changenotifier_mutable_state.problem: ChangeNotifier used mutable state with notifyListeners()
changenotifier_mutable_state.issues: State transitions unclear, hard to debug, breaks time-travel debugging
changenotifier_mutable_state.migration: Convert to AsyncNotifier with immutable state, use state = newValue pattern
